headline: Advance Daily Access Passes Required for Charlevoix Highlands
reservation: Entry to this SÉPAQ park requires a daily access pass which should be purchased online in advance to guarantee entry during peak summer months. Camping and cabin accommodations are managed through a separate inventory and do not include the mandatory daily vehicle or person access fees. Visit the official SÉPAQ portal to verify current seasonal operating dates for the shuttle system and mountain trails.

days.title: Glacial Valleys and River Vistas

stops.name: Le Riverain Trail
stops.detail: Ascend the valley walls for an expansive view of the Malbaie River winding through the steep glacial gorge.

stops.name: Le Bateau-Mouche
stops.detail: Board a guided river cruise to experience the scale of the highest rock faces in Eastern Canada from the water.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to reach the visitor center; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: Park shuttles typically operate during peak summer to manage traffic in the narrow valley.

days.title: The Acropole des Draveurs Ascent
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Le Draveur Visitor Centre

stops.name: Acropole des Draveurs Trail
stops.detail: Tackle the park's signature strenuous climb to reach three distinct summits overlooking the winding Malbaie River.

stops.name: Côté-Passage Sector
stops.detail: Explore the lower valley floor near the river banks for a recovery walk following the mountain descent.

days.driving: Local park shuttle transit or walking between trailheads; allow 1 hour for transitions.
days.note: The summit trail may close early in the day based on capacity or weather; check the trailhead board.

days.title: Paddling the Malbaie Hinterland
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Équerre Rental Point

stops.name: Malbaie River Canoe Route
stops.detail: Navigate the calm sections of the river to view the steep granite cliffs from a silent, low-angle perspective.

stops.name: Le Belvédère Lookout
stops.detail: A final short walk to a panoramic platform for photos of the valley's distinct 'U' shape.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the return drive to La Malbaie; rural roads may have logging activity.
days.note: Water levels fluctuate; rental availability is subject to seasonal river flow conditions.

intel.title: Visitor Centre Hubs
intel.text: Primary parking is located at Le Draveur, but lots often reach capacity by mid-morning in July. Utilize the mandatory park shuttle if directed by staff at the Saint-Aimé-des-Lacs entrance gate.

intel.title: Deep Valley Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is extremely limited or non-existent once you descend into the gorge. Download topographic maps and SÉPAQ guides before leaving Saint-Aimé-des-Lacs.

intel.title: Last Service Points
intel.text: Final fuel and full-service grocery stores are located in La Malbaie and Saint-Aimé-des-Lacs. There are no refueling stations within the park boundaries or on the immediate access road.

intel.title: Trail Closures
intel.text: The Acropole des Draveurs typically has a cut-off time in the early afternoon to ensure hikers return before dark. Verify the specific daily cut-off at the visitor centre upon arrival.

intel.title: Gravel Road Sections
intel.text: The final approach to the park involves well-maintained gravel roads that can be dusty or muddy. Drive with caution as heavy machinery occasionally uses these shared access routes.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Quebec City Airport and stop in La Malbaie for regional supplies before the final 30-minute drive to the park entrance.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the main roads, but check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved park access roads.
plan.goldenHour: Le Riverain lookout provides exceptional light over the gorge during the late summer afternoon.
